cancer_dependency: High: ~85-90% of human cancers depend on telomerase activity via TERT promoter mutations (C228T/C250T) or gene amplification for replicative immortality
stem_cell_dependency: Critical: Proliferating hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and intestinal crypt base columnar cells require basal TERT activity to maintain minimum telomere reserve and prevent premature senescence
therapeutic_window_evidence: Narrow/Toxic: Complete catalytic ablation (e.g. imetelstat GRN163L) causes high-grade thrombocytopenia and neutropenia due to HSC suppression before tumor telomeres reach critical crisis length; requires long lag phase for telomere erosion
experimental_status: Clinically approved for myelodysplastic syndromes (FDA 2024); limited utility in solid tumors due to marrow toxicity and long kinetic lag phase
citation: Liu et al. (Nature 2022); Shay & Wright (Nat Rev Drug Discov 2019); Platzbecker et al. (Lancet 2024)

cancer_dependency: High: TPP1-mediated recruitment is strictly required for telomerase localization to telomeres in telomerase-positive cancer cells; loss blocks de novo telomere elongation
stem_cell_dependency: Critical: Germline deletion or mutation of TPP1 TEL-patch (e.g. Lys170del) causes Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson syndrome and severe Dyskeratosis Congenita with fatal bone marrow failure
therapeutic_window_evidence: Narrow/Hypothetical: No clinical interface inhibitor exists. Complete interface ablation is predicted to phenocopy germline Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson aplastic anemia. Partial or pulsatile attenuation untested
experimental_status: In vitro and cellular validation only; 0 approved drugs; candidate TELIN-1 demonstrated to be non-physical artifact with zero wet-lab validation
citation: Liu et al. (Nature 2022); Kocak et al. (Genes Dev 2014); Guo et al. (Genes Dev 2014); He et al. (Cell 2021)

cancer_dependency: High: TERC template mutations or competitive oligonucleotide binding stops cancer cell proliferation via synthesis of toxic telomeric repeats or catalytic shutdown
stem_cell_dependency: Critical: TERC haploinsufficiency in humans causes autosomal dominant Dyskeratosis Congenita, pulmonary fibrosis, and early stem-cell exhaustion
therapeutic_window_evidence: Narrow: Toxic telomeric repeat incorporation can induce rapid p53-dependent apoptosis but exhibits off-target marrow suppression and systemic immune toxicity
experimental_status: Investigational antisense oligonucleotides (GRN163L derivative); toxic template mimicry explored in preclinical models
citation: Kim et al. (Cancer Res 2001); Armanios & Blackburn (Nat Rev Genet 2012); Vulliamy et al. (Lancet 2001)

cancer_dependency: High: POT1 loss in cancers with ALT or telomerase dysregulation causes telomere uncapping, chromosome end-to-end fusions, and genomic instability
stem_cell_dependency: Critical: Germline POT1 mutations predispose to familial melanoma, glioma, and chronic lymphocytic leukemia; acute ablation triggers massive DNA damage response (TIFs) and p53-dependent stem cell death
therapeutic_window_evidence: Contraindicated: Complete disruption causes acute telomere deprotection and catastrophic genomic crisis in healthy tissues rather than selective anti-cancer effect
experimental_status: Preclinical mechanistic biology; POT1 peptide antagonists in vitro only
citation: Denchi & de Lange (Nature 2007); Palm et al. (Mol Cell Biol 2009); Robles-Espinoza et al. (Nat Genet 2014)

cancer_dependency: High: ~10-15% of human cancers (sarcomas, glioblastoma multiforme, neuroendocrine tumors) utilize ALT driven by ATRX/DAXX loss and break-induced replication (BIR)
stem_cell_dependency: Zero: Normal human somatic and adult stem cells do not utilize ALT; physiological telomere maintenance is strictly telomerase- or shelterin-dependent
therapeutic_window_evidence: Wide (Theoretical): Tumor-specific vulnerability since healthy adult stem cells show 0 dependence on ALT mechanisms; targeting ATR, BLM, or RAD51AP1 selectively kills ALT cells
experimental_status: Preclinical target validation; ATR inhibitors (berzosertib, elimusertib) evaluated in ALT-positive sarcoma clinical trials
citation: Flynn et al. (Science 2015); Dilley et al. (Nature 2016); Amorim et al. (Clin Cancer Res 2022)

cancer_dependency: Zero (in non-transformed somatic tissues): Somatic cells lack immortalization; transient pulse expands telomere length without transforming normal diploid cells
stem_cell_dependency: Beneficial: Transient extension of telomeres in aged HSCs or pulmonary epithelial progenitors extends replicative lifespan without immortalization or oncogenic transformation
therapeutic_window_evidence: Controllable: Transient synthetic modified mRNA (depleted within 48-72 hours) limits telomere elongation to ~1-2 kb, avoiding permanent replicative competence
experimental_status: Preclinical proof-of-concept in human fibroblasts, CD8+ T cells, and primary human stem cells; in vivo mouse models of pulmonary fibrosis
citation: Ramunas et al. (FASEB J 2015); Povedano et al. (Cell Rep 2015); Bär et al. (EMBO Mol Med 2014)

cancer_dependency: Moderate: Reducing Repeat Addition Processivity (RAP) without blocking telomerase recruitment restricts telomere hyper-elongation in rapid cycling tumor cells
stem_cell_dependency: Permissive: Basal non-processive extension is sufficient to prevent critical telomere uncapping and DNA damage checkpoint activation in slow-cycling stem cells
therapeutic_window_evidence: Moderate (Hypothetical): Exploits kinetic rate differential between rapidly cycling tumor cells (requiring high RAP) and slowly dividing quiescent stem cells
experimental_status: Theoretical and in vitro mutational profiling only (TERT TEN/TRAP loop variants; TPP1 TEL-patch mutants)
citation: Sexton et al. (Mol Cell 2014); Drosopoulos et al. (Mol Cell Biol 2012); Jansson et al. (Nat Struct Mol Biol 2015)
